newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Two Uighurs face execution in China - exiles.
newsitem.headline: Two Uighurs face execution in China - exiles.

text.p: A Uighur exile group said on Wednesday two Uighur religious students arrested over rioting last month in China's unstable northwest province of Xinjiang faced execution on Thursday.

"Two young men, accused of leading the February events, will be executed tomorrow (Thursday)," Mukhiddin Mukhlisi, spokesman for the United National Revolutionary Front of East Turkestan, told Reuters by telephone in Almaty, capital of neighbouring Kazakhstan.

Mukhlisi, who said he received information on the executions from his organisation's "secret sources", named the two Uighurs as Abu Khair and Abdu Medchit, both around 25 years old. The two would probably face a firing squad in Urumqi, regional capital of Xinjiang, Mukhlisi said.

He said the two were arrested on February 7 in Yining, near the border with the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan and last month scene of some of the most violent disturbances in the province since the 1949 communist takeover.
The Front is one of several Uighur organisations fighting for an independent "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, home to a majority of Turkic-speaking Moslems like the ethnic Uighurs.
Information from the remote, closed region of mountain and desert is difficult to verify and often comes days late via traders crossing the China-Kazakh border.
